[00:00] Aisha: okay, starting on time, thanks everyone for joining the Q4 launch readiness sync. we've got 75 minutes. agenda: checklist, incident follow-ups, canary plan, monitoring, and open risks.

[00:25] Sofia: i'll go over the launch messaging and any gating product decisions.
[00:32] Jin: and i'll cover ops and monitoring tweaks we need for the canary.

[00:45] Elena: short update from CTO - we want minimal blast radius, SLOs must be explicit, and Legal needs the SOC2 checklist attached to the runbook, thanks.
[01:02] Aisha: ok, first item - launch checklist. i've uploaded the draft at https://redwood.internal/docs/q4-launch-checklist (note: link internal) - high level items: docs, runbook, postmortem fixes, security sign-off, QA, infra soak. Priya, where are we on the regression matrix?

[01:45] Marco: yes, the quant path had a different kernel selection, i think that changed the attention behaviour slightly under long context. i have a branch that reverts the kernel pick for sequences > 2k but need to validate perf.
[02:05] Tom: that's a risk - if we revert, we might increase latency. we need a tradeoff decision: accept slightly higher latency for correctness, or push a fix to the quant kernels. what's the timeline?
[02:22] Marco: i can run a targeted perf sweep tonight and report back tomorrow morning.
[02:27] Priya: perfect, i can re-run the regression tomorrow afternoon after Marco's sweep.
[02:35] Aisha: add that as an action item.
[02:39] Jin: ops side - for the canary window we need longer trace retention (48h) and a couple new alarms: KV cache memory > 85% and prefix cache miss rate spike. i'm going to add a dashboard widget and a Playbook entry.
[02:55] Aisha: good, please also include the backout steps in the runbook. Martina, what's your preferred canary window?
[03:05] Martina: prefer low-traffic weekend window but we want to avoid blackouts; proposing Thu night 11/11 to Fri morning 11/12 so we have on-call coverage.
[03:18] Elena: ensure we have SLA fallbacks - e.g., auto-route to hosted model pool if Dedicated capacity falters.
[03:30] Tom: we have a fallback policy but need to test it end-to-end. Marco, can you simulate a capacity failure?
[03:38] Marco: yes, i can trigger a simulated GPU OOM and watch the routing switch. will validate with the new batching config.
[03:46] Tom: also running the 24h soak with the new batching config starts tomorrow at 02:00 UTC. we'll post the telemetry to the perf dashboard. expected throughput target is 25k tokens/sec sustained.
[04:05] Aisha: what are the acceptance criteria for the canary?
[04:10] Sofia: acceptance criteria: SLOs within 2% of baseline for latency, error rate < 0.5%, no critical regressions in QA, and successful fallback test.
[04:23] Aisha: ok put that in the checklist.
[04:28] Priya: one more QA note - we saw an intermittent 502 when the prefix cache filled. it's reproducible with high concurrency on the quant path. Jin, could that be an NBMI or network flapping?
[04:43] Jin: likely an edge case in cache eviction. i'll instrument the cache metrics and surface the eviction logs. also will increase the connection pool timeouts by 200ms for the canary.
[04:58] Speaker 2 (Tom): question re: rollout percent - do we start at 5% or 10%? ops prefers 5%. product maybe 10% to catch user-level issues faster.
[05:12] Sofia: 5% is safer given the quant path unknowns. we can double to 10% after 4 hours if metrics look good.
[05:20] Elena: agree, start 5% then escalate.
[05:25] Aisha: next - incident review follow-ups from the recent outage. i summarized postmortem items in the doc: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-10-29-cache-eviction. main items: better monitoring, more graceful fallback, and a release gating rule.
[05:48] Marco: we fixed the immediate bug but we need an automated test for eviction under load.
[05:54] Priya: i'll add a regression test that simulates eviction and validates request integrity.
[05:58] Jin: ops will add a runbook entry for immediate mitigation (scale up gpus, route traffic) and a pager flow change.
[06:10] Aisha: security sign-off - Daniel?
[06:13] Daniel: Legal asked for SOC2 checklist, and we need to attest that no unencrypted logs leave the VPC during the canary. I'll coordinate with Security and upload the checklist; recommend sign-off by 11/10.
[06:28] Aisha: ok, add that as a hard gating item.
[06:32] Speaker 3 (interrupt): there was a note about cost impact with the new batching config - do we have estimates?
[06:39] Tom: preliminary numbers show token cost increases ~8% at peak due to lower packing efficiency; but overall latency SLO improves by ~15ms. cost/perf tradeoff needs product approval.
[06:54] Sofia: i think the latency improvement is worth it for user-facing flows. we can limit the config to low-latency routes only to control spend.
[07:06] Aisha: good idea. action - Tom to produce a short cost vs latency summary for product review.
[07:12] Tom: noted.
[07:15] Aisha: last section - comms and launch messaging. Sofia please confirm release notes, support playbook and in-app messaging.
[07:25] Sofia: release notes drafted; support playbook needs a runbook summary, i'll sync with Martina to ensure support knows the fallback options.
[07:33] Martina: will coordinate support coverage and confirm the on-call schedule for canary night.
[07:38] Aisha: recap and next steps: Tom running 24h soak, Marco kernel/perf sweep, Priya QA regression, Jin ops alarms and trace retention, Daniel security SOC2, Martina confirm canary window. i'll consolidate checklist and distribute. any final comments?
[07:58] Elena: please make sure execs get a short one-pager pre-canary.
[08:04] Aisha: will send. thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.
